title: Componentwise normalization under smooth pullback
statement:
Let $f:X	o Y$ be a smooth morphism of locally Noetherian schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Write $
u_X:X^
u	o X$ and $
u_Y:Y^
u	o Y$ for their componentwise normalizations [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. There is a unique isomorphism of $X$-schemes
$$X^
u\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ X	imes_Y Y^
u,$$
where the right side has its first projection to $X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. In particular, this holds for an etale morphism $f$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Neither finite normalization nor excellence is assumed; nonreduced and empty schemes are allowed.

source.place: Tag 07TD, lemma-normalization-and-smooth; locally Noetherian specialization of its finite-irreducible-components hypothesis.

proof.text:
Put $P=X	imes_Y Y^
u$ with projections $p:P	o X$ and $q:P	o Y^
u$. By lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-generic-properties, $Y^
u$ is normal and $
u_Y$ is integral. Base changing this integral morphism along $f$ shows that $p$ is integral. We also retain from that same statement the generic-point bijection for $
u_Y$ and the canonical isomorphism $Y^
u	imes_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$ for each generic point $\eta$ of $Y$. Its hypothesis is satisfied because $Y$ is locally Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 07TD, lemma-normalization-and-smooth, proof; generic-point argument expanded without first passing to reductions.

proof.text:
The projection $q$ is smooth by smooth base change, applied to $f$ along $
u_Y$. Since $Y^
u$ is normal, lem-sfb-smooth-normal-ascent makes $P$ normal. Moreover $f$ and $q$ are flat by lem-pc-smooth-flat. The smooth base change and normal-ascent statements apply to arbitrary schemes: no local Noetherianity of $Y^
u$ or $P$ has been asserted or used.

source.place: Tag 07TD, lemma-normalization-and-smooth, proof; generic-point argument expanded without first passing to reductions.

proof.text: For either flat morphism $f$ or $q$, a generic point of the source maps to a generic point of the target. Indeed, at such a source point the source local ring has only one prime. The corresponding map of local rings is flat by def-weil-flat-morphism. If its target point were not generic, a prime strictly below the maximal ideal of the target local ring would, by lem-sc-flat-going-down, lift below the unique prime of the source local ring. Its contraction would then be both the smaller prime and the maximal ideal, a contradiction. Thus generic points of $X$ lie over generic points of $Y$, while generic points of $P$ map under $q$ to generic points of $Y^\nu$ and hence under $f p=\nu_Y q$ to generic points of $Y$.

source.place: Tag 07TD, lemma-normalization-and-smooth, proof; generic-point argument expanded without first passing to reductions.

proof.text: For a generic point $\eta$ of $Y$, base change of the isomorphism in step 1 gives $P_\eta\simeq X_\eta$ over $X_\eta$. Let $\xi$ be generic in $X$; step 3 gives $f(\xi)=\eta$ generic in $Y$. A further base change gives $P\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$, so there is exactly one point $z$ over $\xi$ and its residue field is $\kappa(\xi)$. This $z$ is generic: any generalization maps to a generalization of the generic point $\xi$, hence to $\xi$ itself, and the fibre has only one point. Conversely, let $z$ be generic in $P$. By step 3 its image in $Y$ is some generic $\eta$. In the isomorphic fibres $P_\eta\simeq X_\eta$, the image $\xi=p(z)$ has no strict generalization. Every generalization of $\xi$ in $X$ still lies over $\eta$ because $\eta$ has no strict generalization, hence $\xi$ is generic in $X$. These assertions about generalizations in a generic fibre are the affine localization description: for a minimal prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, the primes of $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ correspond to primes of $B$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$, and strict inclusions among them are preserved. Thus $p$ gives a bijection on generic points and an isomorphism on their residue fields.

source.place: Tag 07TD, lemma-normalization-and-smooth, proof; generic-point argument expanded without first passing to reductions.

proof.text:
Apply lem-sfb-integral-normal-generic-recognition to $a=p:P	o X$. The base $X$ is locally Noetherian by hypothesis, $p$ is integral by step 1, $P$ is normal by step 2, and the generic-point bijection and residue-field isomorphisms are step 4. It supplies a unique isomorphism $P\simeq X^
u$ over $X$. Taking inverses gives exactly the unique isomorphism $X^
u\simeq X	imes_Y Y^
u$ in the statement; inversion is a bijection between isomorphisms in the two directions. No finiteness of normalization is required. If $X$ is empty, both sides are empty and the same argument has vacuous generic-point conditions. Nonreduced schemes were retained throughout by using residue fields at generic points. All uses of lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-generic-properties concern $Y$, not the possibly non-Noetherian $P$.

source.place: Tag 07TD, lemma-normalization-and-smooth, proof; generic-point argument expanded without first passing to reductions.

proof.text: An etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] is smooth of relative dimension zero in the sense of def-sbc-smooth-morphisms by lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres; in particular it is smooth, so the result just proved applies to the etale case as well.
